encounter.text: The source of the hum: a chamber carved — not built, carved — into the bedrock below the sewers. In the centre, a stone lattice the height of a rat, vibrating at a frequency you feel in your back teeth. Around its base: ash, offerings, things that were once alive. The lattice is not a machine. It is a door. And it is not fully closed.

shut.text: You press your weight against the lattice. It resists — not physically, but in the way a sound resists being silenced. For a moment the hum intensifies, then drops an octave. The gap narrows. Not closed. Not open. Waiting. You step back, ears ringing.

leave.text: You back away carefully. The hum follows you for three tunnels before fading. Whatever is on the other side of that door — it noticed you.
